subject: business-studies
title: Lean Production: JIT vs JIC
welcome_lead: Cut waste with lean - but balance JIT against the risk of stockouts.
meta_desc: A-Level Operations: lean production, JIT, JIC, Kaizen.
final_note: Lean delivers cost and quality gains only when the whole supply chain plays along.

walkthroughs.body_html: Lean targets the seven wastes: overproduction, waiting, transport, inappropriate processing, inventory, motion and defects. The goal is to make only what customers want, when they want it.
JIT cuts stockholding costs and forces quality improvement but is vulnerable to supplier failure - the 2020 chip shortage hit JIT auto plants hard. JIC trades higher costs for resilience.
Kaizen empowers shop-floor staff to suggest small ongoing improvements. Over time hundreds of tiny gains outpace one big project - Toyota credit Kaizen for much of their productivity edge.

mcqs.q: What is operations management concerned with?
options: Operations management is the same as general management.
Productivity is the number of employees a business has.
Operations management is only about manufacturing factories.
The design and control of the production process and business operations — converting inputs into outputs efficiently. It includes capacity, quality, supply chain, and process improvement.
Productivity is the number of employees a business has.
Taylor invented the assembly line at Ford.
Productivity is the total amount produced by a business.
Output per unit of input (per worker, per hour) — measuring efficiency, not total output. A small efficient firm can be more productive than a large inefficient one.
